name: Charles Kains-Jackson
bio: London solicitor specialising in literary matters (1857-1933), and from 1888 to 1894 editor of The Artist and Journal of Home Culture - a magazine which, in the editors' own words, he used in part as a forum for London's homosexual coterie, and to which Lord Alfred Douglas contributed. Wilde consulted him professionally over Salomé in November 1893.
bio_note: the volume's Index of Recipients. THE DESCRIPTION OF HIS MAGAZINE IS THE EDITORS' OWN AND IS QUOTED RATHER THAN PARAPHRASED - 'which he used in part as a forum for London's homosexual coterie' (printed 574, note 1). TWO ITEMS at printed 574 and 576; ONE read at the page. HIS OWN CIRCLE - the Uranian poets, and his editorship's place in that literature - lies outside this volume and is not asserted here.

sources.quote: Can you come and see me here tomorrow at eleven. Wish to consult you professionally on Salomé business.
sources.context: Telegram, Wilde to Charles Kains-Jackson, 6 November 1893, 7.32 p.m., St James's Street (MS Clark) - quoted whole. The editors note that on the verso someone has written 'Reply - that C. K.-J. will keep appointment'. THE SALOMÉ BUSINESS is the dispute over whether Douglas's name should appear as translator on the title page; it was settled by dedicating the play to him instead - 'To my friend Lord Alfred Bruce Douglas, the translator of my play' - after Douglas wrote that the difference was 'between a tribute of admiration from an artist and a receipt from a tradesman'.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That Wilde used him as his solicitor at the height of the Salomé dispute.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 626; printed folio 574 confirmed on the rendered page image.
